svg.title: A Dataverse background operation from request to result
svg.desc: Three lanes: client, Dataverse and an optional callback receiver. Step 1: the client sends POST cedar_RequestDispatch with the header Prefer: respond-async. Step 2: Dataverse answers 202 Accepted immediately, with a Location header for the status monitor resource under /api/backgroundoperation and the header x-ms-dyn-backgroundoperationid; a row exists in the backgroundoperations table with state Ready and status Waiting For Resources; nothing has run. The client may disconnect. Step 3: later the custom API's plug-in runs as the caller, within the two-minute limit; on an error the platform retries up to three times with exponential backoff; the row moves to Locked and In Progress and then to Completed with Succeeded, Failed or Canceled. Step 4: the client sends GET to the status monitor, at most once a minute, and after success reads the output parameters Result and RequestedOn; or Dataverse posts state and status without outputs to the callback URL; or a step registered on OnBackgroundOperationComplete reacts. DELETE on the status monitor cancels only before the operation starts. Rows expire after 90 days by default. The feature is in preview.
svg.text: Background operation (preview): accepted now, run later, read when ready
3. Later: the custom API's plug-in runs
as the caller, within the 2-minute limit
error → up to 3 retries, exponential backoff
Locked / In Progress → Completed / Succeeded | Failed
4a. GET the status monitor (at most once a minute)
4b. POST callback: state + status, no outputs
Cancel: DELETE the status monitor, only before the operation starts. Rows expire after 90 days by default.
Asynchronous does not mean longer: the plug-in limit stays two minutes. Callers need Read and Write on the Background Operation table.
